Overview

Zagreb as a Business Centre

Zagreb is Croatia's capital and the centre of its corporate, financial and administrative life. The city had 767,131 residents at the 2021 census, an estimated 774,000 in 2024, and about 473,000 people in employment in March 2024, with unemployment of 2.4 percent. Zagreb-based companies generated about 49 percent of all Croatian business revenue in 2021, according to the financial agency FINA. City GDP was about 22.3 billion euros in 2022. Zagreb is home to the head offices of most large Croatian groups, banks and insurers, as well as government ministries and national regulators, and Franjo Tuđman Airport handled about 4.3 million passengers in 2024.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Zagreb because almost every significant Croatian transaction or dispute leads back to the capital. Acquirers and lenders need reliable background on Zagreb holding companies, their owners and their political or commercial connections. Groups restructured after privatisation or insolvency often have complex histories that matter to buyers and creditors. Contractors and investors in publicly funded projects face procurement and conflict-of-interest risks centred on national and city authorities. Zagreb is also a base for companies trading with Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia and Slovenia, so counterparties' regional structures and related companies often need to be traced.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Zagreb

01

Croatian group ownership research

Mapping the holding structures, beneficial owners, directors and related companies of Zagreb-headquartered groups ahead of acquisitions, financing or partnerships, using the court register, filed financial statements and Croatian-language sources to show who controls a business and how it connects to other companies.

02

Restructured and insolvent group histories

Researching the history of Zagreb groups that have passed through pre-bankruptcy, bankruptcy or extraordinary administration, including asset transfers, creditor settlements and the background of new owners, for buyers, lenders and creditors assessing continuing liabilities and reputational exposure.

03

Public procurement and conflict checks

Background research on contractors, subcontractors and consortium partners bidding for national ministry, state company or City of Zagreb contracts, looking for undisclosed relationships with officials, prior procurement disputes and adverse media, to support compliance teams and counsel.

04

Regional counterparty tracing

Tracing Zagreb companies' affiliates and shareholders in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Slovenia and Montenegro, where groups commonly operate across borders, to verify trading partners, distributors and investors and to identify relationships not visible from Croatian records alone.

05

Asset research for enforcement

Assembling public information on assets, related companies and property holdings of Zagreb debtors for counsel enforcing judgments or arbitral awards, including recognition proceedings before the Commercial Court in Zagreb, using lawful registry and court sources.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Zagreb

Commercial Court in Zagreb

Croatia has nine commercial courts, and the court in Zagreb handles the largest volume of company matters. Commercial courts keep the court register of companies, decide on formation, operation and dissolution of companies, conduct pre-bankruptcy and bankruptcy proceedings, and recognise foreign judgments and arbitral awards in commercial matters. Their register entries and insolvency files are core public records for Zagreb counterparty research.

High courts seated in Zagreb

Several national appellate courts sit in Zagreb. The High Commercial Court hears appeals from all commercial courts and resolves jurisdictional disputes among them. The High Administrative Court hears appeals from the four administrative courts and reviews general acts, and the High Misdemeanour Court hears misdemeanour appeals. Appellate decisions help establish how a counterparty's disputes were finally resolved.

Permanent Arbitration Court

The Permanent Arbitration Court at the Croatian Chamber of Economy, based in Zagreb, is the country's principal institutional arbitration body, and the Chamber also offers mediation and other alternative dispute resolution services. Domestic and international commercial disputes involving Croatian parties are often administered there. Investigative support is limited to factual research for counsel and the parties.

National regulators and agencies

Zagreb hosts the Croatian Financial Services Supervisory Agency (HANFA), the Croatian National Bank, the Zagreb Stock Exchange and the financial agency FINA, which collects annual financial statements. The State Attorney's office for suppressing corruption and organised crime (USKOK) is also based in the city. Published decisions and disclosures from these bodies are useful public records on listed companies and their management.

Land registry and property

Real property in Zagreb is recorded in the land registry kept by the municipal courts and linked with the cadastre through a joint information system, which allows ownership and encumbrances to be checked. Property records are valuable for asset research, although recent transfers to related parties and incomplete historic records mean findings should be read with the help of Croatian counsel.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Zagreb

For matters touching Zagreb, TDSC first identifies the decision or dispute the work must serve and which Croatian records are relevant: court register entries, FINA financial statements, insolvency files, land registry data and published decisions of national regulators. Research is conducted from Nashville in Croatian and English, extending to Bosnian, Serbian and Slovenian sources where groups operate regionally. Where document retrieval, interviews or local enquiries are justified, TDSC coordinates with appropriately licensed Croatian professionals and the client's counsel rather than acting directly. Personal data is handled under the GDPR with a defined purpose and minimised collection, and findings are presented so that Croatian counsel can use them before Zagreb courts or arbitral tribunals.

TDSC has no office in Zagreb. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Zagreb: Frequently Asked Questions

Where are Zagreb company records kept?

Companies are entered in the court register maintained by the commercial courts, with Zagreb's court handling the city's companies. Annual financial statements are filed with FINA. Together these show directors, members of limited liability companies in many cases, capital and financial performance. We combine them with insolvency, land registry and media sources to build a full profile.

Can you research a Zagreb group that went through restructuring?

Yes. Restructuring and bankruptcy files at the commercial courts, creditor settlements, published decisions and press coverage often document asset transfers and ownership changes. We reconstruct that history so buyers and creditors understand which entities hold the assets now, who controls them and what liabilities or disputes may remain.

Do you support arbitrations at the Croatian Chamber of Economy?

We provide counsel with sourced factual research on the opposing party, its group structure, related companies, financial position and prior disputes, plus asset information relevant to enforcement. We do not contact arbitrators or witnesses improperly, and procedural and legal questions remain with Croatian or international counsel.

Can you check links between a bidder and public officials?

We can research public records, corporate filings, asset declarations where published and media reporting for connections between bidders, their owners and officials involved in a procurement. We report documented links and clearly separate them from inference. Any suspected wrongdoing is a matter for counsel and the competent Croatian authorities.

Does TDSC have an office in Zagreb?

No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Zagreb or elsewhere in Croatia. Most work is desk-based research. Where local steps are needed, we coordinate with appropriately licensed Croatian professionals and the client's counsel, and we decline requests involving pretexting, covert surveillance or access to restricted records.
